title: A Homecoming for the Locker
premise: Three years ago, Noor Amberdale's anonymous code exposed a predatory teacher at Halloway Prep — and got an innocent janitor fired instead. Now his best friend Theo, who knows Noor's secret, vanishes leaving only a locker key, and Noor discovers Theo was investigating the real predator's return. Following the key through the school's forgotten basement lockers, Noor uncovers evidence that could clear the janitor and condemn the man he failed to stop. When the school closes ranks and Theo's disappearance is ruled a runaway case, Noor must choose between staying safely anonymous or going public at last. He testifies under his own name, the truth lands, Theo is found alive but changed, and Noor learns that survival without justice was never really survival.
about_author: Bram Dunmore is a former high-school debate coach from coastal Maine who writes stories about teenagers who refuse to look away. His novels explore the quiet courage of ordinary kids, and he still keeps a locker key on his keyring as a reminder of the student who inspired this book.

chapters.title: The Careful Life
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Three years after his anonymous exposé, Noor lives by rigid rules: no social media, no signatures, no names. At Halloway Prep's reunion assembly, he sees Mr. Vess — the man he failed to expose — back on staff under a new title. The beat is dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Theo misses their Friday ritual, then misses school for three days. Police call it a runaway case; Theo's mother finds nothing missing except a set of keys left deliberately on the windowsill. One key bears a tag Noor recognizes: B-14, the basement lockers. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Locker B-14
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, night scene. Noor breaks into the school basement and opens B-14. Inside: Theo's notebook documenting Vess's pattern of 'transfers' across three schools, plus a printout of the old anonymous post — annotated in red: 'I know it was you.' Beat: betrayal braided with terror.

chapters.title: The Janitor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Marisol Reyes, daughter of the wrongly fired janitor, now works nights cleaning Halloway. She recognizes Noor lurking and confronts him. She has her own file of complaints nobody read. Beat: two guilty survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback chapters within: how Theo figured out Noor wrote the post, promised to keep the secret, and started his own investigation when Vess returned. A text arrives from Theo's number: one word — 'basement.' Beat: hope that curdles into a trap's shape.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They stake out the basement; instead of Theo they find a fresh camera, newly installed, aimed at B-14. Someone is watching the watchers. Noor realizes whoever took Theo wanted the notebook — and now wants its author. Beat: paranoia closing in.

chapters.title: Rules of Anonymity
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor's old contact, a journalist named Ada Quist who once ran his story, warns him: go public and you lose everything safe. Noor weighs his mother's fragile health, his scholarship, his invisibility. Beat: the cost of silence made explicit.

chapters.title: Vess, Up Close
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Vess corners Noor after class with a friendly offer to 'help find Theo,' mentioning the basement cameras casually — too casually. The menace is entirely deniable. Noor plays dumb while his hands shake. Beat: the predator's mask, seen clearly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Other Schools
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Road-trip chapter: the pair drive to Vess's previous schools, collecting sealed records and one brave former student, Priya, willing to talk off-record. Patterns confirm Theo's notebook. Beat: grief for every warning that went unread.

chapters.title: Runaway
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Police close Theo's case officially. Theo's mother, shattered, asks Noor if he knew anything. He lies to her face and hates himself. That night he almost burns the notebook. Beat: the temptation to be small again.

chapters.title: Priya's Testimony
chapters.summary: Priya POV (single chapter). She recounts what Vess did to her at fifteen and why she stayed silent — the scholarship threat, the disbelief of adults. Her voice gives Noor's mission a face. Beat: witness as inheritance.

chapters.title: Trace
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Using his coder skills, Noor pings Theo's phone one last time before the SIM dies: a signal near the abandoned rail depot outside town. He and Marisol scout it and find Theo's jacket. Beat: proof of life, proof of danger.

chapters.title: Ada's Condition
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Quist agrees to run the story only with a named source. She shows Noor what happened to anonymous whistleblowers whose claims died unverified. Noor drafts a confession statement and can't send it. Beat: the pen heavier than any key.

chapters.title: The Assembly
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Vess is honored at a school assembly for 'twenty years of service.' Marisol stands up mid-ceremony and says the truth aloud; she is escorted out, suspended from her job. Beat: the first crack in the wall, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: What They Took From Theo
chapters.summary: Theo POV (recovered journal entries). Interleaved with present: Theo confronted Vess alone, was threatened, ran not away but into hiding to protect Noor, leaving the keys as a trail only Noor would follow. Beat: friendship decoded too late.

chapters.title: Depot
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Acting on the journal's clues, Noor returns to the depot at dusk and finds Theo alive, hiding, injured but lucid — Vess never touched him; he couldn't risk it. But Vess knows where Theo is. Headlights sweep the yard. Beat: reunion inside a countdown.

chapters.title: Cornered
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax part one. Vess arrives with a school-board ally to retrieve the notebook and bury everything. Noor livestreams the confrontation from the shadows — voice only, face hidden, one last act of anonymity used as a weapon. Beat: turning fear into leverage.

chapters.title: Name On the Record
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax part two. The stream forces an investigation, but lawyers circle. To make it stick, Noor walks into Quist's office and signs his name to the original exposé and the new testimony. His mother watches the broadcast. Beat: the labels come off.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Vess is arrested; the board resigns; Marisol is reinstated with an apology that feels thin. Priya comes forward publicly. Some classmates thank Noor; others call him a traitor to the school. Beat: justice arriving imperfect, arriving anyway.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Quiet aftermath: therapy sessions, his mother's anger and pride, Theo's guilt over leaving the keys instead of telling him sooner. Noor admits the three careful years were a slow drowning. Beat: honest accounting.

chapters.title: Reyes v. Halloway
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her father's wrongful-termination suit finally goes to hearing; Noor testifies in open court, name spoken aloud twice. The janitor is cleared. Marisol and Noor stand outside the courthouse, lighter by exactly the weight of their secrets. Beat: restoration.

chapters.title: A Homecoming
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, final chapter. Spring semester: Theo returns to school, Noor co-founds a student accountability collective, and the basement lockers are converted into a memorial wall for voices ignored. Noor leaves his old burner phone inside B-14 and locks it forever. Beat: homecoming not to a place, but to himself.
